intro: Use your own account. Server permissions apply to every request. Schedules shown to Faculty and Students are Published and scoped to their linked identities.

Coordinator: Enter active master data and term-specific weekly/exam slots. Preview CSV imports before confirming.
Create or clone a named configuration, check hard constraints, then generate a new version. The time budget includes startup, input loading, solving and saving.
Adjust only Generated versions. Labs move as complete blocks. Locks survive regeneration from the latest eligible version. Undo restores all tracked changes to the captured baseline.
Approver: Choose a term and Generated version in Review & publish. Review conflicts and room/seat allocations.
Publishing independently validates frozen inputs and freshness, records your approval, and archives the previous Published version for that term and schedule type.
You may review master data, but cannot modify it. Stale inputs require Coordinator regeneration.
Faculty: Your account must link to an active instructor. You may read and change only that instructor’s availability.
View permitted Published timetables and exams. Select the term and version, then export your authorized scope.
Student: Your account must link to a batch. View only that batch’s Published schedules.
Choose a term/version, use course/date filters and download your permitted PDF or CSV.
Administrator: Create accounts, assign roles and trusted instructor/batch links, activate/deactivate accounts and issue password resets in Users & audit.
Password, role, status or identity-link changes revoke sessions. Retrieve authoritative audit events; logs cannot be edited or deleted through the application.
Administrators cannot generate or approve schedules.

screens: Dashboard
Only permitted schedules/actions are shown. Inventory is for administrative reviewers; Faculty and Students use their Published schedule views.
Data management
Choose the correct term before offerings, enrollments or slots. Weekly intervals must be chronological, equal length and non-overlapping. Adjacent lab slots must also touch in clock time.
Import CSV

Download the server template for one of six supported data types. Use UTF-8, exact headers, department codes and at most 10 MB. Preview reports invalid row numbers. Confirmation revalidates and atomically persists accepted rows; no data is saved by preview.
Availability
Faculty may access only their linked instructor. Coordinators may manage instructor availability. Mark unavailable/blocked periods before generation.
Constraints

Save names, seed, time limit and rules together. Mandatory H01/H02/H03/H08/E01/E04/E05 cannot be disabled. Soft weights: 0–10. S03/S04 parameters: 1–12; E02: 1–5. Unused configurations can be deleted; referenced configurations must be retained. Clone to experiment.
Generate

Select term, schedule type and configuration. The progress bar shows elapsed budget, not solved percentage. Cancellation goes to the server; wait for acknowledgement. Timeout and worker failure do not prove infeasibility. Retry only after reviewing diagnostics.
Timetable / Exams

Choose the term and version explicitly. Parallel classes stack in a cell; labs repeat with a continuation marker across occupied cells. Clock windows are those saved with that version. Published/Archived schedules are read-only. CSV/PDF uses current filters and permitted batch/instructor scope.
Review & publish
Only Approvers publish or archive. Publication uses independent snapshot validation and rejects stale or untrusted legacy contexts. Reloading uses persisted server state.
Conflicts
Filter severity and constraint type. A failed/expired run may show interruption diagnostics rather than a proof that no solution exists. The existing conflict CSV is separate from schedule exports.
Users & audit / Password
Use real account administration and audit filters. Change your own password from the account menu. A password reset or account/role change requires signing in again. Never share bearer tokens.
